sk-efcc65cb.stem: Which muscle attaches to the mastoid process?
sk-efcc65cb.explanation: The SCM arises from the sternum and clavicle and attaches to the mastoid process and the lateral part of the superior nuchal line. The mastoid process is absent at birth and develops in childhood under the pull of the muscle.

sk-299c3612.stem: Which structure does NOT pass through the foramen magnum?
options: Spinal root of the accessory nerve
sk-299c3612.explanation: The medulla oblongata and its meninges, the vertebral and spinal arteries and the spinal roots of the accessory nerve pass through the foramen magnum. The internal jugular vein begins at the jugular foramen.

sk-94a4fb4f.stem: Where does the sphenoidal sinus open into the nasal cavity?
sk-94a4fb4f.explanation: The sphenoidal sinus opens into the sphenoethmoidal recess above and behind the superior concha. The posterior ethmoidal cells open into the superior meatus; the frontal, maxillary and anterior ethmoidal sinuses into the middle meatus; the nasolacrimal duct into the inferior meatus.

sk-f4bad9ce.stem: Which muscles attach to the lateral plate of the pterygoid process of the sphenoid?
options: Tensor veli palatini and levator veli palatini
sk-f4bad9ce.explanation: The lower head of the lateral pterygoid arises from the outer surface of the lateral plate and the deep head of the medial pterygoid from its inner surface. The tendon of tensor veli palatini turns around the hamulus at the tip of the medial plate.

sk-24639fbf.stem: Which is the thickest wall of the orbit?
sk-24639fbf.explanation: The lateral wall, formed by the zygomatic bone and greater wing of the sphenoid, is the thickest. The thinnest is the medial wall with the lamina papyracea of the ethmoid; blow-out fractures most often involve the floor.

sk-fe9c4d6f.stem: Which nerve passes through the inferior orbital fissure?
sk-fe9c4d6f.explanation: The maxillary nerve enters the orbit from the pterygopalatine fossa through the inferior orbital fissure and becomes the infraorbital nerve. The frontal, lacrimal, trochlear and abducens nerves pass through the superior orbital fissure.

sk-50fc7e36.stem: Which opening connects the pterygopalatine fossa with the middle cranial fossa?
sk-50fc7e36.explanation: The maxillary nerve (V2) passes from the middle cranial fossa to the pterygopalatine fossa through the foramen rotundum. The foramen ovale and spinosum open into the infratemporal fossa.

sk-c03603d8.stem: Between the two halves of which bone is the metopic suture?
sk-c03603d8.explanation: At birth the frontal bone is in two halves; the metopic suture between them usually closes at 1–2 years. In some adults it remains open and can be mistaken for a fracture line on X-ray.

sk-af9c3b69.stem: Between which bones does the posterior fontanelle lie?
options: The two parietal bones and the occipital bone
The two frontal and two parietal bones
sk-af9c3b69.explanation: The triangular posterior fontanelle lies at the lambda, between the two parietal bones and the occipital bone, and closes at 2–3 months. The anterior fontanelle lies at the bregma between the frontal and parietal bones.

sk-7e5d8299.stem: At which vertebral level does the hyoid bone usually lie?
sk-7e5d8299.explanation: The hyoid lies at the level of C3. The upper border of the thyroid cartilage corresponds to C4 and the cricoid cartilage to C6.

sk-337e8167.stem: Which group of teeth is absent in the primary (deciduous) dentition?
sk-337e8167.explanation: The primary dentition has 20 teeth: in each half-jaw 2 incisors, 1 canine and 2 molars; there are no deciduous premolars. The permanent premolars erupt in place of the deciduous molars.

sk-acf4fff3.explanation: The first permanent tooth to erupt, behind the deciduous teeth, is the 1st molar (the 'six-year molar'); the last is the 3rd molar (wisdom tooth).

sk-5476a288.stem: A heart-shaped body and a small round vertebral foramen are typical of which vertebrae?
sk-5476a288.explanation: Thoracic vertebrae have a heart-shaped body and a small round vertebral foramen; there are facets for the ribs on the body and transverse processes. In cervical vertebrae the foramen is triangular and wide.

sk-6bfe54be.stem: Which are the primary curvatures of the vertebral column?
sk-6bfe54be.explanation: The thoracic and sacral kyphoses, remnants of the fetal C-shaped curve, are the primary curvatures; the cervical and lumbar lordoses develop after birth (secondary curvatures).

sk-a4798013.stem: Through which intervertebral foramen does the L4 spinal nerve exit?
sk-a4798013.explanation: In the thoracic and lumbar regions the spinal nerves exit below the vertebra of the same number; the L4 nerve is in the L4–L5 foramen. A posterolateral L4–L5 disc herniation, however, usually compresses the next root, L5.

sk-d8cdddd6.stem: Which muscle attaches to the rough area (tuberosity) on the outer surface of the 2nd rib?
sk-d8cdddd6.explanation: The 2nd rib is atypical: it is twice as long as the 1st and has a tuberosity on its outer surface for the first digitation of serratus anterior. Pectoralis minor attaches to ribs 3–5, scalenus anterior and subclavius to the 1st rib.

sk-b9394d0e.stem: With the arms hanging at the sides, the inferior angle of the scapula corresponds to which vertebral level?
sk-b9394d0e.explanation: The superior angle of the scapula lies at T2, the medial end of its spine at T3 and the inferior angle at T7. The inferior angle is used as a surface landmark in chest examination and thoracentesis.

sk-c935a47a.stem: With which part of the ulna does the trochlea of the humerus articulate?
sk-c935a47a.explanation: The pulley-shaped trochlea of the humerus fits into the trochlear notch of the ulna between the olecranon and coronoid process, forming the humeroulnar hinge joint. The capitulum articulates with the head of the radius.

sk-fffabda4.stem: Which muscle attaches to the radial tuberosity?
sk-fffabda4.explanation: The biceps brachii tendon attaches to the radial tuberosity below the neck of the radius, which makes it a powerful supinator. Brachialis attaches to the ulnar tuberosity, pronator teres to the middle of the lateral surface of the radius.

sk-afaac4c9.stem: Which are the lateral (radial) attachments of the flexor retinaculum?
options: Tubercle of the scaphoid and tubercle of the trapezium
sk-afaac4c9.explanation: The flexor retinaculum attaches laterally to the tubercles of the scaphoid and trapezium and medially to the pisiform and hook of hamate, forming the roof of the carpal tunnel.

sk-63af94e3.stem: The skin dimples at the lower back (dimples of Venus) mark which bony landmark, at which vertebral level?
options: Highest point of the iliac crest – L4
sk-63af94e3.explanation: The dimples over the sacroiliac region mark the PSIS and correspond to S2; this level is also where the dural sac and subarachnoid space end.

sk-736237ad.stem: Which muscle attaches to the pectineal line of the femur?
sk-736237ad.explanation: Pectineus arises from the pecten pubis and attaches to the pectineal line below the lesser trochanter. Iliopsoas attaches to the lesser trochanter, gluteus maximus to the gluteal tuberosity.
